source_evidence: Institutional Shares (Class I) may have some of the lowest ongoing operating expenses, but there could be relatively high initial investment minimums and/or transaction fees
question: What costs or access limitations might an investor encounter with Institutional Shares (Class I)?
answer: Class I shares may have low ongoing operating expenses, but investing directly through a brokerage account could involve a relatively high initial minimum or transaction fees. Some funds also make Class I available to retail investors through options such as an employer retirement plan or an investment advisory account.
